Read @TASK.md fully. It is a test task: add role-aware access control (Admin, Manager, Member) to this FastAPI full-stack template. Treat the app as already deployed with a populated database.

Do not write any application code in this session step. Work in three phases.

Phase 1, analysis (read-only). Use the superpowers brainstorming skill. Explore the repo and report briefly:
- how auth works today: token creation, what the JWT contains, how get_current_user and the superuser dependency work, where is_active is checked
- every place is_superuser is read or written (backend, frontend, generated client, tests, seed data, migrations)
- how the frontend guards routes and decides what to show in navigation
- existing CI workflows and which of them can run in a repo without deploy secrets
- how the existing test suites are run

Phase 2, decisions. Ask me the open design questions ONE AT A TIME. For each: 2 or 3 options, trade-offs, your recommendation. Wait for my answer before the next one. Cover at least:
- role representation (enum column vs permissions table) and what happens to is_superuser (drop, keep as derived, keep temporarily)
- migration mapping for existing users, and downgrade behavior
- how role and is_active changes reach users with an existing session
- where authorization checks live (dependencies, a single policy module) so one rule can be changed in one place
- last-admin protection, admin changing their own role or active status
- who can see and manage items owned by other users
- blocking role escalation through signup, update-me and any private endpoints
- how the frontend learns the access rules and what an unauthorized direct navigation shows
- how a reviewer gets three users locally
- which security-critical behaviors get automated tests (keep the list short)

Phase 3, after all decisions are made, write two files and stop:
1. CLAUDE.md, under 60 lines: project commands, the decisions we made, and these working rules:
   - Scope: only what TASK.md requires. No unrelated refactoring, no new infrastructure, no visual polish, no extra docs.
   - Priorities for every change: correctness, security, maintainability, consistency with existing template patterns, migration safety, scope control.
   - Clean code: authorization logic in one place, separated from route handlers and UI components, readable names, no duplication of rules between files.
   - Git flow: one feat/* branch per plan step, branched from dev. Small conventional commits. Merge to dev only when tests and lint pass and review findings are resolved. master receives only one final PR from dev. Never commit directly to dev or master.
   - CI: reuse the existing GitHub Actions workflows. Only adjust triggers so tests and lint run on PRs to dev and master. Do not add new pipelines.
   - Per step: write the failing test first for security-critical behavior, implement, then dispatch a separate code-review subagent that checks the diff against the six priorities above. Fix findings before merging.
   - Tools: modern-web-guidance for frontend work, playwright skill and Chrome for verifying the three roles in the browser, Perplexity only for a specific question the repo and official docs cannot answer.
   - Ask me before any decision not covered here.
2. docs/implementation-plan.md, under 60 lines, using the superpowers writing-plans skill: 3 to 5 ordered steps, each with its branch name, files touched, tests to add, and a done-check. The migration with its test comes first, backend authorization second, frontend after.

Commit both files on a feat/rbac-plan branch and show me the plan for approval.

# Ender Turing Full-Stack Developer Test Task

This assignment is for a developer role at Ender Turing.

Add role-aware access control to the existing [Full-Stack FastAPI Template](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/tree/master): https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/tree/master

The stack is FastAPI, SQLModel, PostgreSQL, React and TypeScript.

Prioritize working, understandable code. There is no bonus for extensive documentation, diagrams, agent configuration, generated reports or a large number of tests.

## Product requirements

Introduce three access levels:

* Admin can manage users and their access.
* Manager can view users and metrics, but cannot change user access.
* Member can access and update their own profile.

The metrics page may be a simple stub. Existing application features should keep working unless a change is necessary for the new access model.

Authorization must be enforced by the backend. The frontend should reflect the same access rules and handle direct navigation to unauthorized pages sensibly.

For behavior that is not specified, make reasonable assumptions and implement them consistently.

## Existing production context

Treat the template as an already deployed application, not a new project:

* The database contains existing users created with the current `is_superuser` model.
* Existing data must survive the migration without unintended privilege changes.
* Access or active-status changes must affect users who already have a session.
* Assume migrations run against a populated database.

You decide how roles or permissions are represented, how compatibility is handled, where authorization checks live, and how the backend and frontend communicate access information.

## Expected implementation

* A database migration for any schema changes.
* Backend and frontend behavior for all three access levels.
* Focused automated tests for the security-critical behavior you consider most important.
* A minimal way for the reviewer to exercise all three access levels locally.
* Existing project setup and test commands should continue to work. If your changes require different commands, update the relevant instructions.

Keep the change focused. Unrelated refactoring, infrastructure work and visual polish are outside the task.

## Deliverables

Provide only:

1. A GitHub repository or pull request containing the working implementation and its commit history.
2. The commands needed to run the solution and its tests, if they differ from the original template.
3. The complete raw export of every AI coding conversation used for the task, committed under `ai-conversations/`.

The AI export must contain the original prompts and responses. A summary, retelling, selected excerpts or generated description of the conversation is not a replacement for the raw export. Remove secrets if necessary and mark any redactions clearly.

The code is the primary deliverable. We will review correctness, security, maintainability, consistency, migration safety, scope control, and how the AI tool was directed and validated.

Be prepared to explain the implementation and make a small change to an access rule during a follow-up conversation.

# Full Stack FastAPI Template

[![Test Docker Compose](../../actions/workflows/test-docker-compose.yml/badge.svg)](../../actions/workflows/test-docker-compose.yml)
[![Test Backend](../../actions/workflows/test-backend.yml/badge.svg)](../../actions/workflows/test-backend.yml)

## Technology Stack and Features

- ⚡ [**FastAPI**](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com) for the Python backend API.
  - 🧰 [SQLModel](https://sqlmodel.tiangolo.com) for the Python SQL database interactions (ORM).
  - 🔍 [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev), used by FastAPI, for the data validation and settings management.
  - 💾 [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org) as the SQL database.
- 🚀 [React](https://react.dev) for the frontend.
  - 🧩 Built into the backend application and served by FastAPI on the same domain as the API.
  - 💃 Using TypeScript, hooks, [Vite](https://vitejs.dev), and other parts of a modern frontend stack.
  - 🎨 [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com) and [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com) for the frontend components.
  - 🤖 An automatically generated frontend client.
  - 🧪 [Playwright](https://playwright.dev) for end-to-end testing.
  - 🦇 Dark mode support.
- ☁️ [FastAPI Cloud](https://fastapicloud.com) for deployment.
- 🐋 [Docker Compose](https://www.docker.com) for local services and self-hosted deployment.
  - 📞 [Traefik](https://traefik.io) as a reverse proxy with automatic HTTPS.
- 🔒 Secure password hashing by default.
- 🔑 JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication.
- 📫 Email-based password recovery.
- ✉️ [React Email](https://react.email) for email templates.
- 📬 [Mailpit](https://mailpit.axllent.org) for local email testing during development.
- ✅ Tests with [Pytest](https://pytest.org).
- 🏭 CI (continuous integration) and CD (continuous deployment) based on GitHub Actions.

### Dashboard Login

![Dashboard login screenshot](img/login.png)

### Dashboard - Admin

![Admin dashboard screenshot](img/dashboard.png)

### Dashboard - Items

![Items dashboard screenshot](img/dashboard-items.png)

### Dashboard - Dark Mode

![Dark mode dashboard screenshot](img/dashboard-dark.png)

### React Email Templates

![Email templates screenshot](img/react-email.png)

### Mailpit - Local Email Testing

![Mailpit screenshot](img/mailpit.png)

### Interactive API Documentation

![API docs](img/docs.png)

## How to Use It

Click the **Use this template** button at the top of this page to create a new repository.

## Backend Development

Backend docs: [backend/README.md](./backend/README.md).

## Frontend Development

Frontend docs: [frontend/README.md](./frontend/README.md).

## Deployment

FastAPI Cloud deployment: [deployment.md](./deployment.md).

Self-hosted deployment with Docker Compose: [deployment-docker-compose.md](./deployment-docker-compose.md).

## Development

General development docs: [development.md](./development.md).

This includes the local FastAPI and Vite workflow, Docker Compose services, `.env` configuration, and more.

## Release Notes

Check the file [release-notes.md](./release-notes.md).

## License

The Full Stack FastAPI Template is licensed under the terms of the MIT license.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.
