tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
tools.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
tools.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
tools.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

content.text:
# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
entries.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

```typescript
  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

# Writing Good Tests

**Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or
adding cleanup/helper methods for tests.

## Overview

A test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything
here:

```
1. Every test names the break it catches
2. Every test exercises the real thing
```

Strict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched
failing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns
a mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.

## Principle 1: Name the Break

Before writing the test body, answer: **what production change should
make this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test
earns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong
argument, boundary case, or broken contract.

**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked
fixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred
shape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —
passes no matter what that code does:

```typescript
// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true
const expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });
expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);

// ✅ Hand-derived literal
expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:"urgent"');
```

**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —
a constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires
on redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on
the decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but "a failing call is
retried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens."

**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config
contains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run
scripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or
exit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming
agent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no
test at all.

**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at
its boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload
you produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write
(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that
is the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely
surprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the
assumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,
getters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they
validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —
otherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.

### Gate Function

```
BEFORE writing the test body:
  Name the production change that would make this test fail.

  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior
  "The source text changed"  → run the artifact and assert its effects
  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior
                               that depends on the decision

  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.
  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:
    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture
```

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
exclude = ["venv", ".venv", "alembic"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py314"
exclude = ["alembic"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle errors
    "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
    "B",  # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "ARG001", # unused arguments in functions
    "T201",   # print statements are not allowed
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long, handled by black
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "W191",  # indentation contains tabs
    "B904",  # Allow raising exceptions without from e, for HTTPException
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pyupgrade]
# Preserve types, even if a file imports `from __future__ import annotations`.
keep-runtime-typing = true

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["app"]
dynamic_context = "test_function"

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
sort = "-Cover"

[tool.coverage.html]
show_contexts = true

[tool.ty.terminal]
error-on-warning = true

[tool.fastapi]
entrypoint = "app.main:app"
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "prek>=0.5.3,<1.0.0",
    "typer>=0.27.2,<1.0.0",
    "zizmor>=1.30.1",
]

github-actions = [
    "smokeshow >=0.5.0",
]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["backend"]

[tool.typos.files]
extend-exclude = [
    "img/",
    "uv.lock",
    "bun.lock",
    "backend/coverage/",
    "backend/htmlcov/",
    "backend/app/frontend/",
    "frontend/dist/",
    "frontend/public/assets/images/",
]

[tool.typos.default]
extend-ignore-re = [
    # GitHub usernames in @mentions
    "@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:-?[a-zA-Z0-9])*",
    # Name of the package in the PR title
    "Bump certifi ",
]

[tool.typos.default.extend-identifiers]
alls = "alls"
"""${message}

Revision ID: ${up_revision}
Revises: ${down_revision | comma,n}
Create Date: ${create_date}

"""
from alembic import op
import sqlalchemy as sa
import sqlmodel.sql.sqltypes
${imports if imports else ""}

# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
revision = ${repr(up_revision)}
down_revision = ${repr(down_revision)}
branch_labels = ${repr(branch_labels)}
depends_on = ${repr(depends_on)}


def upgrade():
    ${upgrades if upgrades else "pass"}


def downgrade():
    ${downgrades if downgrades else "pass"}

import uuid
from collections.abc import Generator
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config
from pydantic import PostgresDsn
from sqlalchemy import Connection, Engine, create_engine, inspect, text
from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine as app_engine

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
# Last revision in which privilege is still stored in user.is_superuser
PREVIOUS_REVISION = "fe56fa70289e"


@pytest.fixture
def scratch_engine(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Generator[Engine]:
    """
    Engine for a throwaway database that Alembic is pointed at for one test.

    The migrations never touch the database shared by the rest of the suite.
    """
    name = f"migration_test_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    url = make_url(str(settings.DATABASE_URL)).set(database=name)
    admin_engine = app_engine.execution_options(isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT")
    with admin_engine.connect() as connection:
        connection.execute(text(f'CREATE DATABASE "{name}"'))
    engine = create_engine(url)
    # app/alembic/env.py reads the URL from settings on every run
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        settings,
        "DATABASE_URL",
        PostgresDsn(url.render_as_string(hide_password=False)),
    )
    try:
        yield engine
    finally:
        engine.dispose()
        with admin_engine.connect() as connection:
            connection.execute(text(f'DROP DATABASE "{name}" WITH (FORCE)'))


def alembic_config() -> Config:
    config = Config(str(BACKEND_DIR / "alembic.ini"))
    config.set_main_option("script_location", str(BACKEND_DIR / "app" / "alembic"))
    return config


def upgrade(revision: str) -> None:
    command.upgrade(alembic_config(), revision)


def downgrade(revision: str) -> None:
    command.downgrade(alembic_config(), revision)


def user_columns(engine: Engine) -> set[str]:
    return {column["name"] for column in inspect(engine).get_columns("user")}


def insert_user(connection: Connection, **columns: object) -> None:
    values = {"id": uuid.uuid4(), "hashed_password": "not-a-real-hash", **columns}
    names = ", ".join(values)
    placeholders = ", ".join(f":{name}" for name in values)
    connection.execute(
        text(f'INSERT INTO "user" ({names}) VALUES ({placeholders})'), values
    )


def test_upgrade_maps_superusers_to_admin_and_keeps_is_active(
    scratch_engine: Engine,
) -> None:
    upgrade(PREVIOUS_REVISION)
    with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="active-superuser@example.com",
            is_active=True,
            is_superuser=True,
        )
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="inactive-superuser@example.com",
            is_active=False,
            is_superuser=True,
        )
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="normal-user@example.com",
            is_active=True,
            is_superuser=False,
        )

    upgrade("head")

    assert "is_superuser" not in user_columns(scratch_engine)
    with scratch_engine.connect() as connection:
        rows = connection.execute(text('SELECT email, role, is_active FROM "user"'))
        users = {email: (role, is_active) for email, role, is_active in rows}
    assert users == {
        "active-superuser@example.com": ("admin", True),
        "inactive-superuser@example.com": ("admin", False),
        "normal-user@example.com": ("member", True),
    }


def test_insert_without_role_gets_member(scratch_engine: Engine) -> None:
    upgrade("head")

    with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
        insert_user(connection, email="no-role@example.com", is_active=True)

    with scratch_engine.connect() as connection:
        role = connection.execute(text('SELECT role FROM "user"')).scalar_one()
    assert role == "member"


def test_unknown_role_is_rejected(scratch_engine: Engine) -> None:
    upgrade("head")

    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError, match="ck_user_role"):
        with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
            insert_user(
                connection,
                email="unknown-role@example.com",
                is_active=True,
                role="superuser",
            )


def test_downgrade_restores_is_superuser_only_for_admins(
    scratch_engine: Engine,
) -> None:
    upgrade("head")
    with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
        insert_user(
            connection, email="admin@example.com", is_active=True, role="admin"
        )
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="inactive-admin@example.com",
            is_active=False,
            role="admin",
        )
        insert_user(
            connection, email="manager@example.com", is_active=True, role="manager"
        )
        insert_user(
            connection, email="member@example.com", is_active=True, role="member"
        )

    downgrade(PREVIOUS_REVISION)

    assert "role" not in user_columns(scratch_engine)
    with scratch_engine.connect() as connection:
        rows = connection.execute(
            text('SELECT email, is_superuser, is_active FROM "user"')
        )
        users = {email: (is_superuser, is_active) for email, is_superuser, is_active in rows}
    assert users == {
        "admin@example.com": (True, True),
        "inactive-admin@example.com": (True, False),
        "manager@example.com": (False, True),
        "member@example.com": (False, True),
    }

import uuid
from collections.abc import Generator
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config
from pydantic import PostgresDsn
from sqlalchemy import Connection, Engine, create_engine, inspect, text
from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine as app_engine

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
# Last revision in which privilege is still stored in user.is_superuser
PREVIOUS_REVISION = "fe56fa70289e"


@pytest.fixture
def scratch_engine(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Generator[Engine]:
    """
    Engine for a throwaway database that Alembic is pointed at for one test.

    The migrations never touch the database shared by the rest of the suite.
    """
    name = f"migration_test_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    url = make_url(str(settings.DATABASE_URL)).set(database=name)
    admin_engine = app_engine.execution_options(isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT")
    with admin_engine.connect() as connection:
        connection.execute(text(f'CREATE DATABASE "{name}"'))
    engine = create_engine(url)
    # app/alembic/env.py reads the URL from settings on every run
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        settings,
        "DATABASE_URL",
        PostgresDsn(url.render_as_string(hide_password=False)),
    )
    try:
        yield engine
    finally:
        engine.dispose()
        with admin_engine.connect() as connection:
            connection.execute(text(f'DROP DATABASE "{name}" WITH (FORCE)'))


def alembic_config() -> Config:
    config = Config(str(BACKEND_DIR / "alembic.ini"))
    config.set_main_option("script_location", str(BACKEND_DIR / "app" / "alembic"))
    return config


def upgrade(revision: str) -> None:
    command.upgrade(alembic_config(), revision)


def downgrade(revision: str) -> None:
    command.downgrade(alembic_config(), revision)


def user_columns(engine: Engine) -> set[str]:
    return {column["name"] for column in inspect(engine).get_columns("user")}


def insert_user(connection: Connection, **columns: object) -> None:
    values = {"id": uuid.uuid4(), "hashed_password": "not-a-real-hash", **columns}
    names = ", ".join(values)
    placeholders = ", ".join(f":{name}" for name in values)
    connection.execute(
        text(f'INSERT INTO "user" ({names}) VALUES ({placeholders})'), values
    )


def test_upgrade_maps_superusers_to_admin_and_keeps_is_active(
    scratch_engine: Engine,
) -> None:
    upgrade(PREVIOUS_REVISION)
    with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="active-superuser@example.com",
            is_active=True,
            is_superuser=True,
        )
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="inactive-superuser@example.com",
            is_active=False,
            is_superuser=True,
        )
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="normal-user@example.com",
            is_active=True,
            is_superuser=False,
        )

    upgrade("head")

    assert "is_superuser" not in user_columns(scratch_engine)
    with scratch_engine.connect() as connection:
        rows = connection.execute(text('SELECT email, role, is_active FROM "user"'))
        users = {email: (role, is_active) for email, role, is_active in rows}
    assert users == {
        "active-superuser@example.com": ("admin", True),
        "inactive-superuser@example.com": ("admin", False),
        "normal-user@example.com": ("member", True),
    }


def test_insert_without_role_gets_member(scratch_engine: Engine) -> None:
    upgrade("head")

    with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
        insert_user(connection, email="no-role@example.com", is_active=True)

    with scratch_engine.connect() as connection:
        role = connection.execute(text('SELECT role FROM "user"')).scalar_one()
    assert role == "member"


def test_unknown_role_is_rejected(scratch_engine: Engine) -> None:
    upgrade("head")

    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError, match="ck_user_role"):
        with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
            insert_user(
                connection,
                email="unknown-role@example.com",
                is_active=True,
                role="superuser",
            )


def test_downgrade_restores_is_superuser_only_for_admins(
    scratch_engine: Engine,
) -> None:
    upgrade("head")
    with scratch_engine.begin() as connection:
        insert_user(
            connection, email="admin@example.com", is_active=True, role="admin"
        )
        insert_user(
            connection,
            email="inactive-admin@example.com",
            is_active=False,
            role="admin",
        )
        insert_user(
            connection, email="manager@example.com", is_active=True, role="manager"
        )
        insert_user(
            connection, email="member@example.com", is_active=True, role="member"
        )

    downgrade(PREVIOUS_REVISION)

    assert "role" not in user_columns(scratch_engine)
    with scratch_engine.connect() as connection:
        rows = connection.execute(
            text('SELECT email, is_superuser, is_active FROM "user"')
        )
        users = {email: (is_superuser, is_active) for email, is_superuser, is_active in rows}
    assert users == {
        "admin@example.com": (True, True),
        "inactive-admin@example.com": (True, False),
        "manager@example.com": (False, True),
        "member@example.com": (False, True),
    }

content.text:
Step 1 is implemented and green locally, but the plan has one flaw I need you to decide on before I commit and send it to review: the migration test as we agreed it drops backend coverage to 89%, under the CI gate of 90%.

## The problem

We agreed the migration test would run Alembic inside the pytest process, pointed at the throwaway database by patching `settings.DATABASE_URL`. Because the migration files live under `app/`, running them in-process makes coverage count them for the first time. The five old migrations and `env.py` add 36 uncovered lines (mostly their never-run `downgrade()` functions). The application code itself is at 92%, with the new migration, `models.py` and `crud.py` at 100%.

## Options

**A. Run Alembic as a subprocess in the test (recommended)**
- The test calls the `alembic` CLI with `DATABASE_URL` overridden in the subprocess environment, which is the same path `prestart.sh` uses in production.
- Coverage goes back to counting what it counted before, so the total is 92% with no config change.
- It also removes the `settings` patch and a side effect I'd otherwise have to accept: `env.py` reconfigures logging for the whole pytest process.
- Cost: each Alembic call starts a Python process, so the four tests take a few seconds instead of under one.

**B. Keep it in-process and omit `app/alembic/*` from coverage**
- One line in `backend/pyproject.toml`.
- It changes what the template measures, which is a config change outside the access model.

**C. Keep it in-process and cover the old migrations' downgrades**
- That is writing tests only to raise coverage, which you ruled out.

I recommend A.

## Where step 1 stands

- **Tests:** 62 backend tests pass (the 58 existing ones unedited, plus 4 new migration tests that I watched fail first). Playwright passes 62 of 62, including "Create a superuser" through the shim.
- **Lint:** `scripts/lint.sh` and the pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files. Regenerating the client produces no diff.
- **Local database:** upgrade, downgrade and re-upgrade work with real rows; an inactive admin stays inactive and admin throughout.
- **Not done yet:** nothing is committed, and the review subagent has not run. Both wait on your answer.

## Deviations from the plan

- **Revision id:** the id Alembic generated tripped the repo's spell-check hook, so I renamed the revision to `4f7c2d9e8a13`.
- **`User` table model:** it temporarily declares `email`, `is_active` and `full_name` itself and does not inherit `UserBase`. `UserBase` must keep `is_superuser` in its current position, or the generated client changes field order. Step 2 restores the inheritance.
- **`core/db.py`:** untouched. The shim already maps the seed's `is_superuser=True` to admin, so it changes in step 2.

A, B or C?

A. Constraints:
- Call Alembic as `sys.executable -m alembic` with cwd=backend/, so it uses the same venv as pytest, not whatever alembic is on PATH.
- check=True and capture output; on failure the test must show Alembic's stderr.
- Deviations accepted. Add to the step 2 done-check in the plan: User inherits UserBase again and the temporary field declarations are gone.

Then commit and run the review subagent.

# Role-Aware Access Control: Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Admin, Manager and Member access levels, enforced by the backend and reflected by the frontend, on a populated production database.
**Decisions and rules:** `CLAUDE.md` (numbered decisions D1 to D12). **Spec:** `TASK.md`.
**Every step:** branch from `dev`, failing test first, implement, review subagent, fix findings, then merge when backend tests, Playwright and lint are green.

## Step 1: Role column and migration — `feat/rbac-role-migration`
Schema changes; the API contract does not. All existing tests must pass without edits, which is the proof that nobody's access changed.
- **Files:** `backend/app/models.py` (`Role` StrEnum; `User.role` with server default and CHECK built from the enum; `is_superuser` leaves the table), `backend/app/alembic/versions/<rev>_add_user_role_drop_is_superuser.py` (`down_revision = fe56fa70289e`, order and downgrade per D2, literal role strings because migrations are frozen snapshots), `backend/app/crud.py`, `backend/app/core/db.py`.
- **Temporary shim, fully removed in step 2:** API schemas keep `is_superuser`, so the OpenAPI schema and generated client are unchanged. Read: derived from `role`. Write: one trivial mapping in `crud.py` used by both create and update (`true` to `ADMIN`, `false` to `MEMBER`, unset on update leaves the role alone). No test is written for the shim itself.
- **Tests:** `backend/tests/migrations/test_role_migration.py`. It creates a throwaway database (dropped in fixture teardown even on failure), migrates to `fe56fa70289e`, inserts an active superuser, an inactive superuser and a normal user, upgrades and asserts `admin`, `admin`, `member` with `is_active` unchanged. It then sets one user to `manager`, downgrades and asserts `is_superuser` is true only for admins.
- **Done:** migration test passes; 58 backend and 62 Playwright tests pass unchanged; `generate-client.sh` produces no diff; `alembic upgrade head` then `downgrade -1` then `upgrade head` works on the local populated database.

## Step 2: Backend authorization and API contract — `feat/rbac-backend-authz`
- **Files (backend):** `backend/app/core/permissions.py` (new: `Permission`, `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`, `permissions_for(role)`, `has_permission(user, permission)`, `can_access_item(user, item)`, `can_delete_own_account(user)`, `ensure_active_admin_remains(...)` raising `LastAdminError`), `backend/app/api/deps.py` (`require_permission`; 401 codes per D3; `get_current_active_superuser` removed), `backend/app/api/routes/users.py`, `items.py`, `login.py`, `utils.py`, `backend/app/api/routes/metrics.py` (new stub: user and item counts, behind `metrics:read`), `backend/app/api/main.py`, `backend/app/models.py` (`role` replaces `is_superuser` in API schemas, shim removed; `UserMePublic` with `permissions`), `backend/app/crud.py`.
- **Permission per endpoint:** list users and read another user: `users:read`. Create, update, delete user, test email, password-recovery HTML: `users:manage`. Metrics: `metrics:read`.
- **Files (contract adaptation only, so the frontend still builds):** regenerated `frontend/src/client/`, `frontend/src/lib/permissions.ts` (new: `hasPermission`), `AppSidebar.tsx`, `routes/_layout/admin.tsx`, `routes/_layout/settings.tsx`, `Admin/columns.tsx`, `Admin/AddUser.tsx` and `Admin/EditUser.tsx` (checkbox becomes a role select); `frontend/tests/admin.spec.ts` ("Create a superuser" only).
- **Tests:** `backend/tests/core/test_permissions.py` (every `Role` has an entry). `backend/tests/api/routes/test_access_control.py`: role by endpoint matrix including a manager reading and updating another user's item; a token issued before demotion gets 403 and before deactivation gets 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; signup, update-me and `/private/users/` cannot set `role` or `is_active` (assert database rows); manager and member `PATCH /users/{id}` with `role=admin`, on themselves and on others, get 403 with no change; the only admin cannot be demoted, deactivated or deleted (409), and with two admins one can demote the other. Existing tests that use `is_superuser` switch to `role`; `backend/tests/utils/user.py` gains a create-user-with-role helper.

## Step 3: Frontend access rules — `feat/rbac-frontend-access`

  **1. Medium — Migration safety**
  - **Location**: `backend/app/alembic/versions/4f7c2d9e8a13_add_user_role_and_drop_is_superuser.py`, diff line 40 (`op.drop_column('user', 'is_superuser')`)
  - **Issue**: The same revision adds `role` and drops `is_superuser`, so the schema is incompatible with the previous application code from the moment it commits. An application-only rollback is impossible without running the lossy downgrade.
  - **Failure scenario**: The migration runs while old backend processes are still serving. Every authenticated request selects `user.is_superuser` and returns 500 until the new code is live. This fails closed: nobody gains privilege. If the release is later rolled back, the downgrade must run too, and any managers assigned by then become regular users.
  - **Suggested fix**: Either move the `drop_column` into the step 2 migration (the one that removes the shim), or keep it and state the deploy assumption (stop old code, migrate, start new code) in the migration docstring or PR description.
  - **Confidence**: Verified from the diff for the schema effect. The deploy order is an assumption: check whether the prestart/deploy flow stops the old backend before migrating.
  
  **2. Low — Security (silent privilege change through the shim)**
  - **Location**: `backend/app/crud.py`, diff lines 66-67 and 91-93
  - **Issue**: On update, `is_superuser=false` always writes `Role.MEMBER`, and a manager reads back as `is_superuser=false`. A read-then-write round trip therefore demotes a manager to member.
  - **Failure scenario**: A row has `role='manager'` (only possible by SQL in this step). An admin PATCHes `/users/{id}` with `{"full_name": "X", "is_superuser": false}`, which is what a form that always submits the checkbox sends. The role becomes `member`. This is a demotion only; no input escalates beyond what `is_superuser=true` already granted before.
  - **Suggested fix**: In `update_user`, write the role only when the boolean actually changes: `true` sets ADMIN; `false` sets MEMBER only if `db_user.role == Role.ADMIN`; otherwise leave the role alone.
  - **Confidence**: Verified from the diff for the mapping. Whether the current frontend always sends `is_superuser` on edit is an assumption: check `Admin/EditUser.tsx`.
  
  **3. Low — Correctness (test coverage of the shim)**
  - **Location**: `backend/app/crud.py`, diff lines 91-93; no matching test in the diff
  - **Issue**: The property that prevents unintended privilege change on update (omitted `is_superuser` leaves the role untouched) is not pinned by any test in this diff.

## Summary of step 1

1. **Schema:** migration `4f7c2d9e8a13` adds `user.role` (varchar, NOT NULL, default `member`, CHECK on the three values), maps `is_superuser = true` to `admin`, and drops `is_superuser`. Privilege now has one source of truth, and any insert that sets no role gets the lowest level.
2. **Downgrade:** it restores the original `is_superuser` column exactly, with no leftover default, true only for admins. Managers become regular users, so a rollback can never grant access.
3. **Code:** a `Role` StrEnum and the `role` column on the `User` model, plus a temporary shim that keeps `is_superuser` in the API (derived on read, one mapping in `crud.py` on write). The API and generated client are unchanged, so all 58 existing backend tests and 62 Playwright tests pass unedited.
4. **Tests:** four migration tests run the real Alembic CLI against a throwaway database: the data mapping with `is_active` untouched, default role is `member`, unknown role rejected, and the downgrade. Each was watched failing first.
5. **Review:** the independent review found no critical or high issues. The five confirmed fixes are in, and the plan gained two step 2 checks (`User` inherits `UserBase` again; a partial `PATCH` of an admin keeps the role).

To review the diff yourself: `git diff origin/dev...feat/rbac-role-migration` (6 files, +295 −6, five commits).

Your local database is at the new revision with only `admin@example.com` in it, because the test suite's teardown deletes all users, as it did on the baseline.

"""
Security-critical access rules for the three roles.

Expected results are written out as literals on purpose: they are the access
policy as the product defines it, not values derived from the code under test.
"""

import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable, Generator

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from httpx import Response
from sqlmodel import Session, col, select

from app import crud
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.permissions import Role
from app.models import User, UserCreate
from tests.utils.item import create_random_item
from tests.utils.user import create_random_user, create_user_and_log_in
from tests.utils.utils import random_email, random_lower_string

API = settings.API_V1_STR
Headers = dict[str, str]


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def no_outgoing_email(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr("app.api.routes.users.send_email", lambda **_: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr("app.api.routes.utils.send_email", lambda **_: None)


# --- Role by endpoint matrix -------------------------------------------------


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def headers_by_role(client: TestClient, db: Session) -> dict[Role, Headers]:
    return {
        role: create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=role)[1]
        for role in Role
    }


def new_user_payload() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"email": random_email(), "password": random_lower_string()}


# Each request targets a user or an item that belongs to somebody else.
REQUESTS: dict[str, Callable[[TestClient, Headers, Session], Response]] = {
    "list users": lambda client, headers, _db: client.get(
        f"{API}/users/", headers=headers
    ),
    "read another user": lambda client, headers, db: client.get(
        f"{API}/users/{create_random_user(db).id}", headers=headers
    ),
    "create a user": lambda client, headers, _db: client.post(
        f"{API}/users/", headers=headers, json=new_user_payload()
    ),
    "update another user": lambda client, headers, db: client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{create_random_user(db).id}",
        headers=headers,
        json={"full_name": "Changed"},
    ),
    "delete another user": lambda client, headers, db: client.delete(
        f"{API}/users/{create_random_user(db).id}", headers=headers
    ),
    "read metrics": lambda client, headers, _db: client.get(
        f"{API}/metrics/", headers=headers
    ),
    "send a test email": lambda client, headers, _db: client.post(
        f"{API}/utils/test-email/",
        headers=headers,
        params={"email_to": random_email()},
    ),
    "read password recovery email": lambda client, headers, db: client.post(
        f"{API}/password-recovery-html-content/{create_random_user(db).email}",
        headers=headers,
    ),
    "read another user's item": lambda client, headers, db: client.get(
        f"{API}/items/{create_random_item(db).id}", headers=headers
    ),
    "update another user's item": lambda client, headers, db: client.put(
        f"{API}/items/{create_random_item(db).id}",
        headers=headers,
        json={"title": "Changed"},
    ),
}

# (request, status for admin, status for manager, status for member)
ACCESS_MATRIX = [
    ("list users", 200, 200, 403),
    ("read another user", 200, 200, 403),
    ("create a user", 200, 403, 403),
    ("update another user", 200, 403, 403),
    ("delete another user", 200, 403, 403),
    ("read metrics", 200, 200, 403),
    ("send a test email", 201, 403, 403),
    ("read password recovery email", 200, 403, 403),
    ("read another user's item", 200, 403, 403),
    ("update another user's item", 200, 403, 403),
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("request_name", "role", "expected_status"),
    [
        pytest.param(name, role, status, id=f"{role} - {name}")
        for name, admin, manager, member in ACCESS_MATRIX
        for role, status in (
            (Role.ADMIN, admin),
            (Role.MANAGER, manager),
            (Role.MEMBER, member),
        )
    ],
)
def test_access_matrix(
    client: TestClient,
    db: Session,
    headers_by_role: dict[Role, Headers],
    request_name: str,
    role: Role,
    expected_status: int,
) -> None:
    response = REQUESTS[request_name](client, headers_by_role[role], db)

    assert response.status_code == expected_status


# --- Changes reach users who already have a session --------------------------


def test_demotion_applies_to_an_existing_session(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: Headers
) -> None:
    manager, headers = create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=Role.MANAGER)
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/", headers=headers).status_code == 200

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{manager.id}",
        headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"role": "member"},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200

    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/", headers=headers).status_code == 403
    me = client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers).json()
    assert me["role"] == "member"
    assert me["permissions"] == []


def assert_unauthenticated(response: Response) -> None:
    assert response.status_code == 401
    assert response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] == "Bearer"


def test_deactivation_ends_an_existing_session(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: Headers
) -> None:
    user, headers = create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=Role.MEMBER)
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers).status_code == 200

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{user.id}",
        headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"is_active": False},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200

    assert_unauthenticated(client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers))


def test_deletion_ends_an_existing_session(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: Headers
) -> None:
    user, headers = create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=Role.MEMBER)

    r = client.delete(f"{API}/users/{user.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200

    assert_unauthenticated(client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers))


def test_invalid_token_is_unauthenticated(client: TestClient) -> None:
    headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer not-a-valid-token"}

    assert_unauthenticated(client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers))


# --- No privilege escalation ---------------------------------------------------


def test_signup_cannot_set_role_or_active_status(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    email = random_email()

    r = client.post(
        f"{API}/users/signup",
        json={
            "email": email,
            "password": random_lower_string(),
            "full_name": "Signup User",
            "role": "admin",
            "is_superuser": True,
            "is_active": False,
        },
    )

    assert r.status_code == 200
    user = crud.get_user_by_email(session=db, email=email)
    assert user
    assert user.role == Role.MEMBER
    assert user.is_active is True


def test_update_me_cannot_change_role_or_active_status(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    user, headers = create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=Role.MEMBER)

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/me",
        headers=headers,
        json={"full_name": "New Name", "role": "admin", "is_active": False},
    )

    assert r.status_code == 200
    db.refresh(user)
    assert user.full_name == "New Name"
    assert user.role == Role.MEMBER
    assert user.is_active is True


def test_private_create_user_cannot_set_role(client: TestClient, db: Session) -> None:
    email = random_email()

    r = client.post(
        f"{API}/private/users/",
        json={
            "email": email,
            "password": random_lower_string(),
            "full_name": "Private User",
            "role": "admin",
            "is_superuser": True,
        },
    )

    assert r.status_code == 200
    user = crud.get_user_by_email(session=db, email=email)
    assert user
    assert user.role == Role.MEMBER


@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", [Role.MANAGER, Role.MEMBER])
def test_non_admin_cannot_promote_themselves(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, role: Role
) -> None:
    user, headers = create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=role)

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{user.id}", headers=headers, json={"role": "admin"}
    )

    assert r.status_code == 403
    db.refresh(user)
    assert user.role == role


@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", [Role.MANAGER, Role.MEMBER])
def test_non_admin_cannot_promote_another_user(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, role: Role
) -> None:
    _, headers = create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=role)
    other_user = create_random_user(db)

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{other_user.id}", headers=headers, json={"role": "admin"}
    )

    assert r.status_code == 403
    db.refresh(other_user)
    assert other_user.role == Role.MEMBER


# --- At least one active admin always remains ---------------------------------


@pytest.fixture
def only_active_admin(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> Generator[tuple[User, Headers]]:
    """
    A new admin who is the only active admin while the test runs.

    The other admins in the shared test database are deactivated, not demoted,
    so the tests also show that inactive admins do not count.
    """
    other_admins = db.exec(
        select(User).where(User.role == Role.ADMIN, col(User.is_active))
    ).all()
    for admin in other_admins:
        admin.is_active = False
    db.add_all(other_admins)
    db.commit()
    try:
        yield create_user_and_log_in(client=client, db=db, role=Role.ADMIN)
    finally:
        for admin in other_admins:
            admin.is_active = True
        db.add_all(other_admins)
        db.commit()


def test_only_active_admin_cannot_demote_themselves(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, only_active_admin: tuple[User, Headers]
) -> None:
    admin, headers = only_active_admin

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{admin.id}", headers=headers, json={"role": "member"}
    )

    assert r.status_code == 409
    db.refresh(admin)
    assert admin.role == Role.ADMIN


def test_only_active_admin_cannot_deactivate_themselves(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, only_active_admin: tuple[User, Headers]
) -> None:
    admin, headers = only_active_admin

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{admin.id}", headers=headers, json={"is_active": False}
    )

    assert r.status_code == 409
    db.refresh(admin)
    assert admin.is_active is True


def test_only_active_admin_cannot_delete_themselves(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, only_active_admin: tuple[User, Headers]
) -> None:
    admin, headers = only_active_admin
    admin_id = admin.id

    by_id = client.delete(f"{API}/users/{admin_id}", headers=headers)
    as_me = client.delete(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers)

    # An admin can never delete their own account, whether or not they are the
    # last one, so this is refused before the last-admin rule is consulted.
    assert by_id.status_code == 403
    assert as_me.status_code == 403
    db.expire_all()
    assert db.get(User, admin_id) is not None


def test_admin_can_demote_another_admin_while_one_remains(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, only_active_admin: tuple[User, Headers]
) -> None:
    _, headers = only_active_admin
    second_admin = crud.create_user(
        session=db,
        user_create=UserCreate(
            email=random_email(), password=random_lower_string(), role=Role.ADMIN
        ),
    )

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{second_admin.id}", headers=headers, json={"role": "member"}
    )

    assert r.status_code == 200
    db.refresh(second_admin)
    assert second_admin.role == Role.MEMBER


def test_update_that_omits_role_keeps_the_role(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: Headers
) -> None:
    admin = crud.create_user(
        session=db,
        user_create=UserCreate(
            email=random_email(), password=random_lower_string(), role=Role.ADMIN
        ),
    )

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{admin.id}",
        headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"full_name": "Renamed"},
    )

    assert r.status_code == 200
    db.refresh(admin)
    assert admin.full_name == "Renamed"
    assert admin.role == Role.ADMIN


def test_unknown_user_id_is_not_found(
    client: TestClient, superuser_token_headers: Headers
) -> None:
    r = client.get(f"{API}/users/{uuid.uuid4()}", headers=superuser_token_headers)

    assert r.status_code == 404
