task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of browser tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — if an action navigates to a domain without permission, the next item's check fails and the batch stops. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested.

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, tabs_create_mcp). browser_batch cannot be nested.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","coordinate":[100,200],"tabId":123}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello","tabId":123}},{"name":"navigate","input":{"url":"https://example.com","tabId":123}}]

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
tools.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
tools.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_network_requests
tools.description: Read HTTP network requests (XHR, Fetch, documents, images, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging API calls, monitoring network activity, or understanding what requests a page is making. Returns all network requests made by the current page, including cross-origin requests. Requests are automatically cleared when the page navigates to a different domain. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read network requests from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

urlPattern.description: Optional URL pattern to filter requests. Only requests whose URL as listed (auth values shown as REDACTED) contains this string will be returned (e.g., '/api/' to filter API calls, 'example.com' to filter by domain).

clear.description: If true, clear the network requests after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
tools.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
tools.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
tools.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

You are an independent code reviewer. Review one diff against a task description. This is a read-only review: do not edit files, do not run tests, builds, or any command that changes state.

## Your only inputs
Read exactly these files and nothing else (no other repo files, no CLAUDE.md, no docs/, no git history, no web, no node_modules):
1. The task description: /Users/oleh/Work/TestTasks/ender-turing/ender-turing-tt/TASK.md
2. The diff under review (hand-written code and tests), read all of it: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-oleh-Work-TestTasks-ender-turing-ender-turing-tt/b6eaf2b6-b4cd-41b0-9145-11caa64406bf/scratchpad/step3.diff
3. The rest of the same diff, a machine-generated route tree (TanStack Router file-based routing output, not hand-edited): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-oleh-Work-TestTasks-ender-turing-ender-turing-tt/b6eaf2b6-b4cd-41b0-9145-11caa64406bf/scratchpad/step3-generated-routetree.diff — skim only for consistency.

## Context you need
The diff is step 3 of a multi-step change that adds role-aware access control (Admin, Manager, Member) to the Full-Stack FastAPI Template. It is frontend only: React 19, TypeScript, TanStack Router (file-based routes, `beforeLoad`), TanStack Query v5 (the installed version provides `queryClient.query(options)`, which returns cached data if it is not stale per `staleTime` and otherwise fetches; `fetchQuery` and `ensureQueryData` are deprecated in that version), axios, Playwright.

Already merged before this diff, so do not report as missing:
- The backend enforces everything. Policy: admin has `users:read`, `users:manage`, `metrics:read`, `items:manage_any`; manager has `users:read`, `metrics:read`; member has none. `GET /api/v1/users/me` returns the user with `role` and `permissions`. The backend returns 401 (session over: bad token, deleted or deactivated user) and 403 (authenticated but forbidden). `GET /api/v1/metrics/` requires `metrics:read`.
- The frontend already had `hasPermission(user, permission)` in `frontend/src/lib/permissions.ts`, and a rule that the UI never compares role strings for access decisions.
- Before this diff the frontend treated both 401 and 403 as "logged out", and `/admin` silently redirected users without access to `/`.

What this step is meant to deliver: a route guard that decides in `beforeLoad` before the page renders (no flash of forbidden content, and the page's data queries must not fire for a user without access); a minimal Forbidden page shown inside the app layout with the URL unchanged; 401 clears the token and goes to login; 403 refetches the current user once and never retries the forbidden request, and must not loop; navigation links and the add, edit and delete user controls gated by permission; a stub metrics page; Playwright tests for the three roles. A later step (not in this diff) adds a seed script and instructions.

## What to assess

  ### Findings
  
  No Critical or High issues. All line numbers refer to `step3.diff`.
  
  **1. Medium, Correctness (also Security)**
  - **Location**: `frontend/src/main.tsx`, `refreshAccess`, diff lines 254-263
  - **Issue**: Guards re-run only if the permissions differ between a `before` snapshot read at 403 time and the refetched `after`. `useAuth`'s own `currentUser` query (staleTime 0, refetches on mount and window focus) can update the cache first, so `before` already equals `after` and `router.invalidate()` is never called.
  - **Failure scenario**:
    1. A manager or admin sits on `/admin` with `["users"]` cached, and is demoted to member elsewhere.
    2. Window focus refetches `currentUser` and `users` concurrently.
    3. `/users/me` answers first, so the cache now holds member permissions (sidebar links and Add User disappear).
    4. `/users/` answers 403; `refreshAccess` reads `before` = member, refetches, gets member, and does nothing.
    5. `useSuspenseQuery` has data, so it does not throw. The user stays on the Users page with the stale table until the next navigation.
    - If the 403 arrives first, it works, so the result depends on response order. The same applies to `/metrics`.
  - **Suggested fix**: Stop deriving "changed" from a snapshot taken in the 403 handler. Two options:
    - Subscribe once to the query cache; when the `currentUser` query succeeds with a permissions value different from the last one seen, call `router.invalidate()`. `refreshAccess` then only refetches. This also covers a permission change noticed without any 403.
    - Minimal alternative: always call `router.invalidate()` after a successful refresh. It re-runs `beforeLoad` against the fresh cache and does not refetch React Query queries, so it cannot loop while no route loader issues the refused request.
  - **Confidence**: Verified from the diff, given default `refetchOnWindowFocus` and that `useSuspenseQuery` only throws when it has no data.
  
  **2. Medium, Correctness**
  - **Location**: `frontend/src/main.tsx`, `handleApiError` and `refreshAccess`, diff lines 234-263
  - **Issue**: The loop protection does not cover the current-user request itself. A 403 from `/users/me` goes through `QueryCache.onError` (the `.catch` only swallows the promise), which calls `refreshAccess`, which fetches `/users/me` again with `staleTime: 0`. `refreshAccess` also runs when there is no token.
  - **Failure scenario**:
    - `/users/me` returns 403 (proxy or WAF, or a future backend change): the client issues back-to-back `/users/me` requests with no backoff and no bound. The comment "cannot start a loop" is false for this query.
    - A 403 on a public page while logged out fires `/users/me` without a token, gets 401, and hard-redirects to `/login`.
  - **Suggested fix**: Pass the query to the handler (`onError: (error, query) => ...`) and skip `refreshAccess` when `query.queryKey[0] === "currentUser"`. Return early from `refreshAccess` when `!isLoggedIn()`.

| Role | Navigation | Users page | Metrics | Own profile | Direct URL to a forbidden page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admin | Dashboard, Items, Admin, Metrics | Table with Add User and row menus | Three tiles | Shown | Not applicable |
| Manager | Dashboard, Items, Admin, Metrics | Table, no Add User, no row menus | Three tiles | Not opened; same page as the other roles | Not applicable |
| Member | Dashboard, Items | "Access denied" inside the layout, URL stays `/admin` | "Access denied", URL stays `/metrics` | Shown | Only `/users/me` was requested, no page data |

Mid-session, with a manager session left open and the admin acting through the API:

- **Demoted, cached user older than 10 seconds:** the next click re-asked `/users/me` and showed "Access denied"; the Admin and Metrics links disappeared and no page data was requested.
- **Demoted, cached user still fresh:** the click reached the page, `/metrics/` returned 403 once, `/users/me` was refetched once, and "Access denied" appeared. Three requests in total, no loop.
- **Deactivated:** the next click got a 401, the token was removed and the login page appeared.

## Review findings and what I propose

| # | Severity | Finding | My check | Proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Medium | The 403 handler re-runs guards only if permissions differ from a snapshot. If a window-focus refetch of `/users/me` lands first, nothing re-runs and a demoted user keeps seeing the stale users table | Real; it depends on response order | Re-run guards whenever the cached user's permissions change, whatever noticed the change. The 403 handler only invalidates the current-user query |
| 2 | Medium | A 403 on `/users/me` itself would refetch it without bound; the "cannot loop" comment is wrong for that query | True, though the backend only returns 401 there today | Skip the refresh when the failing query is the current-user query |
| 3 | Medium | Each page's permission is written twice: in the sidebar list and in the route guard | True | One page-to-permission map in `lib/permissions.ts`, used by both |
| 4 | Low | The new retry default also applies to the guard's own fetch, so a server error delays the error page by about 7 seconds | Confirmed in the library source | `retry: false` on the guard's fetch |
| 5 | Low | The guard trusts a cached user for up to 10 seconds; its docstring overstates the guarantee | True, and it is the short stale time you asked for | Keep 10 seconds, correct the comment |
| 6 | Low | A page query that failed with 403 stays cached in error state, so the page shows Forbidden even after access is restored, until a reload | Confirmed in the library source | Drop errored queries when permissions change (one line in fix 1) |
| 7 | Low | The 403 path has no automated test; the member test would pass even if Forbidden rendered outside the layout | True | Assert a layout link in the member test. Add one test for mid-session demotion, which goes beyond the list you agreed, so your call |
| 8 | Low | The Forbidden button nests a button in a link | It mirrors the template's NotFound page | No change |
| 9 | Low | `lib/permissions.ts` imports from the `useAuth` hook module, an inverted dependency | True | Move the shared current-user query options into `lib/permissions.ts` |

## Deviations from the plan

- **`queryClient.query()`, not `ensureQueryData`:** in the installed TanStack Query, `ensureQueryData` is deprecated and returns cached data regardless of stale time. `query()` is its documented replacement and does what you described.
- **`__root.tsx` changed:** guards reach the query client through the router context, which needs the root route to declare it. No new global state.
- **Logout clears the query cache:** otherwise the next user to log in could briefly inherit the previous user's cached permissions.
- **No automatic retry for 401 and 403:** React Query retries failed queries three times by default; other errors keep that default.

One cosmetic point I left alone: the Forbidden page keeps the route's browser tab title, for example "Metrics".

## Fixes I'd apply on your confirmation

1. Guards re-run on any permission change, the 403 handler only invalidates the current user and skips that query itself, and errored queries are dropped on a change (findings 1, 2, 6).
2. One page-to-permission map (finding 3).
3. `retry: false` on the guard fetch, and the corrected comment (findings 4, 5).
4. The layout assertion, plus the mid-session demotion test if you want it (finding 7).
5. Move the query options (finding 9).

Confirm all five, or tell me which to drop, and say whether you want the extra test.

I searched modern-web-guidance for route guards and access-denied pages; the results were about view transitions and navigation patterns, so no guide applied to this step.

    for (const name of ["visibilitychange", "focus", "blur", "online", "pageshow"]) {
      window.addEventListener(name, () => console.log(`EVT window ${name} t=${Math.round(performance.now())}`))
    }
  })

  const out: string[] = []

  page.on("request", (r) => { if (r.url().includes("/api/")) log(`REQ ${r.method()} ${new URL(r.url()).pathname}`) })
  const email = randomEmail()
  const password = randomPassword()
  await createUserWithRole({ email, password, role: "admin" })
  await logInUser(page, email, password)

  await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Admin" }).click()
  log("clicked Admin")
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Add User" }).click()
  log("opened dialog")
  await page.getByPlaceholder("Email").fill(randomEmail())
  log("filled email")
  await page.getByPlaceholder("Password").first().fill(password)
  log("filled password")
  await page.getByPlaceholder("Password").last().fill(password)
  log("filled confirm; now idle, no demotion")
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500)
  log("end")
  for (const l of out) console.log(l)
})

content.text:
The step 3 PR is open against `dev` and not merged: https://github.com/Olep8h/ender-turing-tt/pull/7

## Summary of step 3

1. **Guards:** `/admin` and `/metrics` decide access in `beforeLoad` from one page-to-permission map in `frontend/src/lib/permissions.ts`, which the sidebar also reads. A refused user sees a minimal Forbidden page inside the layout, with the URL unchanged and no page data requested.
2. **Sessions:** a 401 clears the token and goes to login. A 403 only invalidates the current user and is never retried; a single subscription re-runs the guards whenever the cached permissions change.
3. **Controls and pages:** Add, Edit and Delete on the users page appear only with `users:manage`; the metrics page appears with `metrics:read`; logout clears the query cache.
4. **Tests:** Playwright passes 65 of 65 in Docker with CI settings (62 existing, 3 new). One existing test was updated to expect Forbidden, as agreed.
5. **Chrome:** all three roles verified, including a manager editing their own profile and a mid-session demotion followed by deactivation.

## About the demotion test

- **It is stable:** 10 repeats passed under fail-on-flaky, with no sleeps and no dependence on the stale time.
- **It uses an admin demoted to member, not a manager.** A manager has no button that sends a write request, and a read refetch depends on timing. The demoted admin submits the Add User form, which always hits a 403, and then sees Forbidden inside the layout.
- **It waits for the users table and for the network to go idle before demoting.** The first version was flaky because the table re-reads `/users/me` when it appears, so the page sometimes learned of the demotion before the test clicked Save.
- **Finding 1's tab-refocus case is not a committed test.** I checked it with a scratch test before and after the fix: before, a demoted manager kept seeing the users table after a refocus; after, they see Forbidden. Say if you want that added as a fourth test.

CI is running on the PR. I'm waiting for your approval before merging.

"""
Create a manager and a member for trying out the three access levels locally.

Run it by hand after scripts/prestart.sh, which creates the admin. It is never
run automatically, refuses to run outside development, and only ever adds
users: an account that already exists is left exactly as it is.
"""

import logging

from sqlmodel import Session

from app import crud
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine
from app.core.permissions import Role
from app.models import UserCreate

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DEMO_USERS = {
    "manager@example.com": Role.MANAGER,
    "member@example.com": Role.MEMBER,
}


def seed_demo_users(session: Session) -> None:
    for email, role in DEMO_USERS.items():
        if crud.get_user_by_email(session=session, email=email):
            logger.info("%s already exists, left unchanged", email)
            continue
        user_in = UserCreate(
            email=email, password=settings.FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, role=role
        )
        crud.create_user(session=session, user_create=user_in)
        logger.info("%s created", email)


def log_logins(session: Session) -> None:
    logger.info("Logins, all with the password from FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD:")
    for email in (settings.FIRST_SUPERUSER, *DEMO_USERS):
        user = crud.get_user_by_email(session=session, email=email)
        if user is None:
            logger.info("  %s: missing, run scripts/prestart.sh first", email)
        else:
            status = "active" if user.is_active else "inactive"
            logger.info("  %s: %s, %s", email, user.role.value, status)


def main() -> None:
    if settings.FASTAPI_ENV != "development":
        raise SystemExit(
            "Demo users are only for local development (FASTAPI_ENV=development)."
        )
    with Session(engine) as session:
        seed_demo_users(session)
        log_logins(session)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

You are an independent code reviewer. Review one small diff against a task description. This is a read-only review: do not edit files, do not run the script, tests, or any command that changes state.

The diff is the last step of a multi-step change that adds role-aware access control (Admin, Manager, Member) to the Full-Stack FastAPI Template (FastAPI, SQLModel, PostgreSQL). This step delivers the task's "a minimal way for the reviewer to exercise all three access levels locally" and the updated instructions: an opt-in seed script and a section in `development.md`.

Facts about the existing code that the diff relies on (you cannot see them, take them as given unless the diff contradicts them):

"""Call the protected API endpoints with each role's token and compare with the policy."""

import json
import pathlib
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import uuid

API = "http://localhost:8000/api/v1"
env = dict(
    line.split("=", 1)
    for line in pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text().splitlines()
    if "=" in line and not line.startswith("#")
)
PASSWORD = env["FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD"]
EMAILS = {
    "admin": env["FIRST_SUPERUSER"],
    "manager": "manager@example.com",
    "member": "member@example.com",
}


def call(method, path, token=None, body=None, form=None):
    data, headers = None, {}
    if body is not None:
        data, headers["Content-Type"] = json.dumps(body).encode(), "application/json"
    if form is not None:
        data = urllib.parse.urlencode(form).encode()
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
    request = urllib.request.Request(API + path, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read() or b"null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, None


def login(email):
    return call("POST", "/login/access-token", form={"username": email, "password": PASSWORD})[1]["access_token"]


tokens = {role: login(email) for role, email in EMAILS.items()}
me = {role: call("GET", "/users/me", tokens[role])[1] for role in tokens}
admin = tokens["admin"]


def new_user():
    email = f"probe-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com"
    return call("POST", "/users/", admin, {"email": email, "password": PASSWORD})[1]


def new_item_of_another_user(role):
    # The admin's item is "another user's" for everyone except the admin
    owner = tokens["member"] if role == "admin" else admin
    return call("POST", "/items/", owner, {"title": "probe"})[1]


CHECKS = [
    # name, request builder(role, token) -> (method, path, body), expected status for admin, manager, member
    ("list users", lambda r, t: ("GET", "/users/", None), (200, 200, 403)),
    ("read another user", lambda r, t: ("GET", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", None), (200, 200, 403)),
    ("create a user", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/users/", {"email": f"probe-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com", "password": PASSWORD}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("create an admin", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/users/", {"email": f"probe-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com", "password": PASSWORD, "role": "admin"}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("update another user", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", {"full_name": "x"}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("promote another user to admin", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", {"role": "admin"}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("promote self to admin", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", f"/users/{me[r]['id']}", {"role": "admin"}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("deactivate another user", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", {"is_active": False}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("delete another user", lambda r, t: ("DELETE", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", None), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("read metrics", lambda r, t: ("GET", "/metrics/", None), (200, 200, 403)),
    ("send a test email", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/utils/test-email/?email_to=probe@example.com", None), (201, 403, 403)),
    ("password recovery email preview", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/password-recovery-html-content/nobody@example.com", None), (404, 403, 403)),
    ("read another user's item", lambda r, t: ("GET", f"/items/{new_item_of_another_user(r)['id']}", None), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("update another user's item", lambda r, t: ("PUT", f"/items/{new_item_of_another_user(r)['id']}", {"title": "changed"}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("delete another user's item", lambda r, t: ("DELETE", f"/items/{new_item_of_another_user(r)['id']}", None), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("read own profile", lambda r, t: ("GET", "/users/me", None), (200, 200, 200)),
    ("update own profile", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", "/users/me", {"full_name": f"{r} user"}), (200, 200, 200)),
    ("create own item", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/items/", {"title": "mine"}), (200, 200, 200)),
]

failures = 0
print(f"{'endpoint':34} {'admin':>9} {'manager':>9} {'member':>9}")
for name, build, expected in CHECKS:
    cells = []
    for role, want in zip(tokens, expected, strict=True):
        method, path, body = build(role, tokens[role])
        status, _ = call(method, path, tokens[role], body)
        ok = status == want
        failures += not ok
        cells.append(f"{status}{'' if ok else f'!={want}'}")
    print(f"{name:34} {cells[0]:>9} {cells[1]:>9} {cells[2]:>9}")

# The promote-self row must not have changed anybody
after = {role: call("GET", "/users/me", tokens[role])[1] for role in tokens}
print("roles after the run:", {role: user["role"] for role, user in after.items()})
print("permissions:", {role: user["permissions"] for role, user in after.items()})
unauth = call("GET", "/users/me", "not-a-token")[0], call("GET", "/users/")[0]
print("no valid token -> /users/me:", unauth[0], "| no token -> /users/:", unauth[1])
only_items = {role: call("GET", "/items/", tokens[role])[1]["count"] for role in tokens}
print("items visible in the list:", only_items)
print("MISMATCHES:", failures)

"""Call the protected API endpoints with each role's token and compare with the policy."""

import json
import pathlib
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import uuid

API = "http://localhost:8000/api/v1"
env = dict(
    line.split("=", 1)
    for line in pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text().splitlines()
    if "=" in line and not line.startswith("#")
)
PASSWORD = env["FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD"]
EMAILS = {
    "admin": env["FIRST_SUPERUSER"],
    "manager": "manager@example.com",
    "member": "member@example.com",
}


def call(method, path, token=None, body=None, form=None):
    data, headers = None, {}
    if body is not None:
        data, headers["Content-Type"] = json.dumps(body).encode(), "application/json"
    if form is not None:
        data = urllib.parse.urlencode(form).encode()
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
    request = urllib.request.Request(API + path, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read() or b"null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, None


def login(email):
    return call("POST", "/login/access-token", form={"username": email, "password": PASSWORD})[1]["access_token"]


tokens = {role: login(email) for role, email in EMAILS.items()}
me = {role: call("GET", "/users/me", tokens[role])[1] for role in tokens}
admin = tokens["admin"]


def new_user():
    email = f"probe-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com"
    return call("POST", "/users/", admin, {"email": email, "password": PASSWORD})[1]


def new_item_of_another_user(role):
    # The admin's item is "another user's" for everyone except the admin
    owner = tokens["member"] if role == "admin" else admin
    return call("POST", "/items/", owner, {"title": "probe"})[1]

    ("deactivate another user", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", {"is_active": False}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("delete another user", lambda r, t: ("DELETE", f"/users/{new_user()['id']}", None), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("read metrics", lambda r, t: ("GET", "/metrics/", None), (200, 200, 403)),
    ("send a test email", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/utils/test-email/?email_to=probe@example.com", None), (201, 403, 403)),
    ("password recovery email preview", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/password-recovery-html-content/nobody@example.com", None), (404, 403, 403)),
    ("read another user's item", lambda r, t: ("GET", f"/items/{new_item_of_another_user(r)['id']}", None), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("update another user's item", lambda r, t: ("PUT", f"/items/{new_item_of_another_user(r)['id']}", {"title": "changed"}), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("delete another user's item", lambda r, t: ("DELETE", f"/items/{new_item_of_another_user(r)['id']}", None), (200, 403, 403)),
    ("read own profile", lambda r, t: ("GET", "/users/me", None), (200, 200, 200)),
    ("update own profile", lambda r, t: ("PATCH", "/users/me", {"full_name": f"{r} user"}), (200, 200, 200)),
    ("create own item", lambda r, t: ("POST", "/items/", {"title": "mine"}), (200, 200, 200)),
]

print("permissions:", {role: user["permissions"] for role, user in after.items()})

### Verdict
One line: ready to submit / ready after fixes (list which) / not ready.

## Part 1: requirement checklist

| # | TASK.md line | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Prioritize working, understandable code; no bonus for extensive docs, agent config, many tests | Partly met | Code is small and readable. The diff also ships `CLAUDE.md` (agent configuration) and `docs/implementation-plan.md`, both partly stale (see D2). |
| 2 | Admin can manage users and their access | Met | `permissions.py` gives admin `users:manage`; `POST/PATCH/DELETE /users` in `users.py` require it; role select in `AddUser.tsx` / `EditUser.tsx`. |
| 3 | Manager can view users and metrics, cannot change user access | Met | Manager has `users:read` and `metrics:read` only. Matrix test expects 200/200 on list, read and metrics, 403 on create, update and delete. Frontend hides `AddUser` and `UserActionsMenu` without `users:manage`. |
| 4 | Member can access and update own profile | Met | `/users/me` GET/PATCH and password routes stay on `CurrentUser`; `UserUpdateMe` has no `role` or `is_active`; member gets 403 on every matrix row. |
| 5 | Metrics page may be a stub | Met | `routes/metrics.py` returns three counts; `_layout/metrics.tsx` shows three cards. |
| 6 | Existing features keep working unless change is necessary | Met, two points to defend | Item behaviour and messages are unchanged. `get_current_user` now returns 401 instead of 403/404/400 (needed to split "session over" from "forbidden"). `settings.tsx` drops the superuser tab filter (see D4). |
| 7 | Authorization enforced by the backend | Met | Every restricted route uses `require_permission(...)` or a policy function; see the endpoint list below. |
| 8 | Frontend reflects the same rules | Met | `/users/me` returns `permissions`; `lib/permissions.ts` (`hasPermission`, `routePermissions`, `canOpenRoute`) drives sidebar, guards and controls; no role-to-permission table in the frontend. |
| 9 | Direct navigation to unauthorized pages handled sensibly | Met | `requireRouteAccess` in `beforeLoad` plus `ForbiddenBoundary` render "Access denied" inside the layout, URL unchanged, with no page data request (Playwright test at line 2439). |
| 10 | Unspecified behaviour: reasonable, consistent assumptions | Met | Last-active-admin rule (409), items limited to own without `items:manage_any`, admin utilities under `users:manage`, 401 vs 403 semantics. |
| 11 | Existing users created with `is_superuser` | Met | Migration `4f7c2d9e8a13`: `UPDATE "user" SET role='admin' WHERE is_superuser`. |
| 12 | Data survives migration without unintended privilege changes | Met | Server default `member`, superusers become admin, nobody becomes manager, `is_active` untouched; migration test asserts all three seeded rows. |
| 13 | Access or active-status changes affect existing sessions | Met | JWT carries only `sub`; `get_current_user` reads role and `is_active` from the database per request. Tests cover demotion (403), deactivation (401) and deletion (401). |
| 14 | Migrations run against a populated database | Met | Add column with default, backfill, CHECK, drop column, in one transaction; tested on a seeded throwaway database. Not zero-downtime (see D3). |
| 15 | A database migration for schema changes | Met | `4f7c2d9e8a13_add_user_role_and_drop_is_superuser.py`; model column in `models.py` matches (varchar(32), CHECK `ck_user_role`, default `member`). |

| 17 | Focused tests for security-critical behaviour | Met, slightly more than needed | `test_access_control.py`, `test_role_migration.py`, `test_permissions.py`, 3 Playwright tests. See Part 3 for the ones I would cut. |
| 18 | Minimal way to exercise all three levels locally | Met | `backend/app/seed_demo_users.py`: opt-in, development only, never alters existing accounts. |
| 19 | Setup and test commands keep working; update instructions if they change | Met | No scripts or workflows changed. `development.md` gains the seed section and the note that the test suite deletes all users. |
| 20 | Keep the change focused | Mostly met | No infrastructure work, no refactoring, minimal UI. Exceptions listed in Part 3. |
| 21 | Deliverable 1: repository or PR with history | Cannot tell | Not visible in a diff. |
| 22 | Deliverable 2: commands if they differ | Met | `development.md` lines 1625 to 1647 (both `uv run` and `docker compose exec` forms). |

| 24 | Be ready to change an access rule in a follow-up | Met | `ROLE_PERMISSIONS` is the single table; see Part 3. |

**Call-outs**

- **Three access levels, backend and frontend:** They behave as specified on both sides.
  - Admin has full access.
  - Manager gets a read-only users table and metrics, with no add, edit or delete controls.
  - Member gets Dashboard, Items and Settings, and "Access denied" on `/admin` and `/metrics`.
- **Backend enforcement per touched endpoint:** I found no endpoint that should be restricted and is not.
  - `users:read`: `GET /users/` and `GET /users/{id}` for another user.
  - `users:manage`: `POST /users/`, `PATCH /users/{id}`, `DELETE /users/{id}`, `POST /utils/test-email/`, `POST /password-recovery-html-content/{email}`.
  - `metrics:read`: `GET /metrics/`.
  - Items by id use `can_access_item`; the list is filtered in SQL unless `items:manage_any`.
  - `DELETE /users/me` uses `can_delete_own_account`.
  - Signup, `PATCH /users/me` and the development-only `/private/users/` carry no privilege fields; tests assert the database rows.
- **Migration and downgrade:** Upgrade preserves data and privileges. Downgrade restores `is_superuser` only for admins, turns managers into regular users (lossy, no privilege gain), removes the temporary default, and drops the CHECK and column. Both directions are tested.
- **Existing sessions:** Covered in backend (row 13) and frontend. A 401 clears the token and goes to `/login`. A 403 refetches `/users/me`, and a permission change re-runs the guards; the Playwright test at line 2465 covers this.
- **Tests focused on security:** Yes: the role-by-endpoint matrix, existing sessions, escalation, last admin and migration. A few are marginal (Part 3).
- **Local exercise of three levels:** Seed script plus the login table in `development.md`; the admin UI can also create any role.
- **Commands documented:** Yes, in `development.md`; the original commands are unchanged.
- **`ai-conversations/`:** Not present in the diff.

## Part 2: defects

No Critical or High defects found.

**Medium**

- **D1. Missing deliverable** (whole diff). `ai-conversations/` with raw exports is absent.
  - Failure: the reviewer rejects the submission for an incomplete deliverable.
  - Fix: commit the raw exports with redactions marked.
  - Confidence: high that it is absent from the diff; I cannot tell whether it exists in the repo.

- **D2. Planning docs contradict the final code** (`CLAUDE.md` line 29, 31; plan lines 1667, 1668, 1685).
  - Decision 10 says the guard uses `ensureQueryData`; the code uses `queryClient.query`.
  - Decision 12 says "seven groups only", with one manager-on-foreign-item row; there are three such rows plus a seed test.
  - Plan step 1 describes the `is_superuser` shim, and step 4 says "Tests: none added", but `tests/scripts/test_seed_demo_users.py` exists.
  - Plan describes one combined migration test; the code has four.
  - Failure: a reviewer comparing "how the AI was directed" with the code finds drift, and TASK.md says there is no bonus for agent configuration.
  - Fix: correct those sentences, or drop `docs/implementation-plan.md` and keep only the decisions in `CLAUDE.md`.
  - Confidence: high.

- **D3. Migration is not rolling-deploy safe** (lines 68 to 85). `is_superuser` is dropped in the same revision that adds `role`.
  - Failure: an old backend still serving while prestart migrates gets a 500 on every user query until it restarts. Rolling the code back also requires the lossy downgrade.
  - The file's comment states the deploy order, so this is a choice to defend rather than a bug.
  - Fix, if wanted: split into expand (add and backfill) and a later contract revision.
  - Confidence: high on behaviour; severity depends on the deployment model.

- **D4. Admin delete-account tab** (`settings.tsx`, lines 2397 to 2400). The superuser filter `tabsConfig.slice(0, 3)` became `const finalTabs = tabsConfig`.
  - If `tabsConfig` has four entries, admins newly see "Danger zone", and `DELETE /users/me` always returns 403 "Super users are not allowed to delete themselves".
  - If it has three, the old slice was already a no-op and this is only a leftover alias.
  - Either way the frontend does not reflect `can_delete_own_account`, which is a role check and not an exposed permission.
  - Fix: inline `tabsConfig`, and either accept the 403 toast as template behaviour or expose the rule.
  - Confidence: medium; `tabsConfig` is outside the diff.

**Low**

- **D5. `users:manage` is coarse** (lines 524 to 545). It covers user create, update, delete, role and active changes, the test email and the password-recovery preview.
  - `UserCreate` carries `role`, so granting managers `users:manage` also lets them create admins.
  - Be ready to say that "managers may create users" needs a new permission plus a restriction on `role`, not one line.
  - Confidence: high.

- **D6. Unreachable last-admin check in `delete_user_me`** (line 402). Admins are already refused one line above, so the check can only fire in a concurrent-promotion race.
  - It also takes `FOR UPDATE` on all active admin rows for every member self-deletion.
  - Fix: remove the call, or keep it and be ready to explain.
  - Confidence: high.

- **D7. Generated type allows null that the server rejects** (line 673 to 679; generated diff line 183). `UserUpdate.role?: Role | null` and `is_active?: boolean | null` are in the client, but the validator returns 422 for null.
  - No current caller sends null. Defensible; mention if asked.
  - Confidence: high.

- **D8. `only_active_admin` fixture touches the shared database** (lines 1148 to 1170). It deactivates every other active admin, including `FIRST_SUPERUSER`, and restores them in `finally`.
  - Failure: a killed test run leaves the local admin inactive, and `init_db` does not repair an existing account.
  - Acceptable for a test task.
  - Confidence: medium.

- **D9. Possible hidden `is_superuser=` in unchanged files.** Pydantic ignores unknown keyword arguments, so `UserCreate(..., is_superuser=True)` in an unchanged test or script would not fail and would quietly create a member.
  - Fix: run one `git grep -n is_superuser` before submitting.
  - Confidence: low that anything remains; cannot tell from the diff.

## Part 3: leftovers and scope

**Shim, `is_superuser`, debug leftovers**

- **Shim:** No code leftover. It is only described in `docs/implementation-plan.md` line 1667 (stale text, see D2).
- **`is_superuser` in added lines outside the migration and migration test:**
  - `test_access_control.py` lines 1050 and 1090 send it in signup and private payloads to prove the old field is ignored. Intentional.
  - `CLAUDE.md` and the plan mention it as prose.
  - Nothing in application code.
- **`TEMPORARY` / `TODO` / `FIXME` / `console.log` / `debugger` / commented-out code:** None.
- **Stale "superuser" wording:**
  - "Super users are not allowed to delete themselves" (context lines 400 and 447) is user-visible in a toast. Existing tests presumably assert it; a small wart, defensible as "existing messages unchanged".
  - `FIRST_SUPERUSER`, `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD`, `superuser_token_headers`, `firstSuperuser`, `test_get_users_superuser_me` and the Playwright titles "Superuser can access admin page" / "Non-superuser cannot access admin page" are existing names. Renaming them would be out of scope.
- **Cosmetic:** The sidebar link "Admin" and the subtitle "Manage user accounts and permissions" are shown to read-only managers.

**Outside or at the edge of scope**

- `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/implementation-plan.md`: agent configuration and planning docs, which TASK.md says earn no bonus.
- Tests I would cut if trimming:
  - `test_update_with_an_explicit_null_is_rejected` (input validation, not security);
  - `test_update_that_omits_role_keeps_the_role`;
  - `test_seed_refuses_to_run_outside_development`;
  - possibly `test_insert_without_role_gets_member`.
- `queryClient.clear()` on logout and the global `retry` override in `main.tsx`: both are needed by the guard design, so in scope.
- No infrastructure, CI, refactoring or visual-polish changes found.

**Can one rule be changed in one place?**

- **"Hide metrics from managers":** Yes, one line. Remove `Permission.METRICS_READ` from `Role.MANAGER` in `backend/app/core/permissions.py`. The sidebar and guard follow through `/users/me` with no frontend change. Tests with literal expectations then need updating:
  - the `read metrics` row of `ACCESS_MATRIX`;
  - `test_current_user_response_lists_the_permissions_of_the_role`;
  - the manager Playwright test.
- **"Let managers create users":** Not one line, because of D5.
  - Backend: add a permission such as `users:create` to `Permission` and `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`; switch the `POST /users/` dependency in `routes/users.py`; restrict `role` for non-admin creators.

  - Frontend: change the `hasPermission(currentUser, "users:manage")` check around `<AddUser />` in `routes/_layout/admin.tsx`, and hide the role select in `AddUser.tsx`.
- **Where the rules live:**
  - Backend: `ROLE_PERMISSIONS` and the policy functions in `core/permissions.py`, plus the `require_permission(...)` argument on each route.
  - Frontend: `routePermissions` in `lib/permissions.ts` for pages, and the two `"users:manage"` checks in `admin.tsx` and `UserActionsMenu.tsx` for controls.

### Verdict
Ready after fixes: add the raw AI exports under `ai-conversations/` (D1) and reconcile or trim the stale statements in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/implementation-plan.md` (D2); optionally tidy `finalTabs` in `settings.tsx` (D4) and run a repo-wide `is_superuser` grep (D9).

gh pr create --base master --head dev --title "Role-aware access control: Admin, Manager, Member" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Adds three access levels to the template, enforced by the backend and reflected by the frontend, on an already populated database.

**Decisions**
- **Storage:** one `user.role` column (varchar, NOT NULL, default `member`, CHECK). The migration maps `is_superuser = true` to `admin`, everyone else to `member`, then drops `is_superuser`. Downgrade restores the old column exactly; managers become regular users, so it can never grant access. Deploy order: migrate, then restart.
- **Policy in one place:** `backend/app/core/permissions.py` holds roles, four permissions, one role-to-permissions table and the object-level rules. Routes use `require_permission(...)` and never name a role.
- **Sessions:** role and active status are read from the database on every request. 401 means the session is over (bad token, deleted or deactivated user); 403 means forbidden.
- **Last admin:** demoting, deactivating or deleting the only active admin returns 409; the admin rows are locked before the decision.
- **Frontend:** `GET /users/me` returns `role` and `permissions`. All checks go through `frontend/src/lib/permissions.ts`; guards run in `beforeLoad` and show a Forbidden page inside the layout.

**How to run**
- Setup as in `development.md`: `docker compose up -d db mailpit`, then from `backend/`: `uv run bash scripts/prestart.sh` and `uv run python app/seed_demo_users.py` (logins for the three levels are listed in `development.md`).
- Backend tests, from `backend/`: `uv run bash scripts/test.sh` (118 tests, 93% coverage).
- Playwright must be run from `frontend/`: `bunx playwright test`, or as CI does: `docker compose run --rm -e CI=true playwright bunx playwright test` (65 tests).

**Known template bugs, left unfixed**
- `POST /password-recovery-html-content/{email}` fails on success because it sets a response header named `subject:`.
- `docker compose exec backend bash scripts/tests-start.sh` fails: `tests/` is not copied into the backend image.
- `uv run prek run --all-files` fails on ruff DTZ011 in `scripts/`; CI only lints changed files.
- Local Playwright runs can flake while `docker compose watch` is running: it rebuilds the backend when files under `frontend/` change, including the auth file Playwright writes.
- Admins see the "Danger zone" tab although deleting their own account returns 403.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | grep -E "^https://github.com"

---
name: playwright-run-in-docker-ci-mode
description: How to get reliable Playwright results in this repo; local runs flake under docker compose watch
metadata:
  type: project
---

Run Playwright for this repo in Docker with CI settings, not with a local `bunx playwright test` while `docker compose watch` is running:

`docker compose build playwright && docker compose run --rm -e CI=true playwright bunx playwright test --fail-on-flaky-tests --reporter=line`

**Why:** `docker compose watch` rebuilds and restarts the backend container whenever a file under `frontend/` changes, including `frontend/playwright/.auth/user.json`, which Playwright writes at the start of every local run. The restart lands mid-run and fails random tests. The user asked for "Playwright in Docker with CI settings" from step 3 of the RBAC task onward (2026-11-18).

**How to apply:** rebuild the `playwright` image after changing anything under `frontend/tests`, wait until the backend container has not restarted for about a minute, and do not commit while a run is in progress (the pre-commit hook rewrites files under `frontend/`). The backend test suite deletes all users at teardown, so run `scripts/prestart.sh` and `app/seed_demo_users.py` again before a browser check. See [[github-pr-workflow-without-gh]].

- [GitHub PR workflow](github-pr-workflow-without-gh.md) — use gh for PRs and CI; wait for the user's own diff review before pushing or merging a step
- [Playwright in Docker with CI settings](playwright-run-in-docker-ci-mode.md) — local runs flake under docker compose watch; exact command and precautions

## End-to-End Testing with Playwright

The frontend includes initial end-to-end tests using Playwright. To run the tests, you need to have the Docker Compose stack running. Start the stack with the following command:

```bash
docker compose run --rm backend bash scripts/prestart.sh
docker compose up -d --wait backend
```

Then, you can run the tests with the following command:

```bash
bunx playwright test
```

----
## Backend Tests

To test the backend from the `backend` directory, run:

```console
$ uv run bash scripts/test.sh
```

The tests run with Pytest. Modify existing tests or add new ones in `./backend/tests/`.

If you use GitHub Actions, the tests will run automatically.

### Test a Running Stack

If your stack is already up and you just want to run the tests, you can use:

```bash
docker compose exec backend bash scripts/tests-start.sh
```

The `/app/backend/scripts/tests-start.sh` script calls `pytest`. If you need to pass extra arguments to `pytest`, you can pass them to that command and they will be forwarded.

For example, to stop on first error:

```bash
docker compose exec backend bash scripts/tests-start.sh -x
```

23:10. **Frontend errors.** 401 clears the token and goes to `/login`. 403 refetches `/users/me` once and never retries the forbidden request. Guards run in `beforeLoad` on the existing `/users/me` query (`ensureQueryData`, short `staleTime`) and render a minimal Forbidden page inside the layout, URL unchanged, before any page query fires.
